Definition: from G575 and ἀλγέω (to smart); to grieve out, i.e. become apathetic:--be past feeling.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says the Gentiles, being past feeling, have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness. The word names the heart that has grieved itself out, grown numb to what once stung.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for being past feeling carries no doctrine of its own; its terror is Paul's, that a heart can grow so used to sin it no longer feels it.
